_comment: Recovery policy for CHECKOUT ABANDONMENT - a customer who started checkout but never completed a payment attempt at all (no decline_code exists for this category by definition - see BUILD_LOG.md's dated checkout-abandonment section). Mirrors config/decline_policy.json's exact shape: one allowed_action per diagnosed abandonment_reason, edited directly by a merchant with no Python change and no redeploy. What each allowed_action actually does is explained in plain English right below in _action_glossary, same as decline_policy.json.

_action_glossary.immediate_payment_link_resend: Likely a technical hiccup (OTP/3-D Secure delay or failure) - the system immediately re-sends a fresh checkout link, since the underlying problem has probably already cleared by the time this runs.
_action_glossary.payment_link_alternate_methods_nudge: The customer's preferred payment method probably wasn't available or didn't work - the system sends a fresh checkout link whose message highlights the other payment methods accepted (UPI, other cards, netbanking), not just a bare retry.
_action_glossary.discounted_incentive_nudge: The customer likely balked at the price when they saw the total - the system sends a checkout link with a small incentive/discount message attached, to address price sensitivity specifically rather than just repeating the same offer.
_action_glossary.delayed_nudge_no_discount: The customer was probably just distracted/multitasking, not put off by anything about the checkout itself - the system sends a plain reminder with NO discount (nothing to fix, no need to pay them to come back), timed to arrive after they've likely returned to what they were doing.
_action_glossary.no_action_respect_hesitation: The customer showed signs of a genuine trust/security concern about entering payment details. The system takes NO automated action at all and leaves it to a human/marketing team to decide - an automated nudge to someone already hesitant about security risks looking pushy or, worse, more suspicious, not helpful.
_action_glossary.no_action_low_value: The abandoned cart's value is below the threshold where an automated recovery message is worth sending at all (messaging cost/customer-annoyance risk outweighs a very small cart's value) - not a per-reason policy, this is applied by the enforcement layer regardless of diagnosed reason.
_action_glossary.no_action_stale_abandonment: Too much time has passed since the cart was abandoned for a nudge to still be the right call (the review-then-buy window has almost certainly closed) - applied by the enforcement layer regardless of diagnosed reason, mirroring gate.py's stale-halt escalation rule for subscriptions.
_action_glossary.no_action_needs_human_review: A hard-block fallback (spending cap exceeded, or a duplicate action already run this session) - not a reason-driven policy choice, applied by the enforcement layer exactly like gate.py's own hard-block fallback action.

_note_simulated_recovery_rate: simulated_recovery_rate is used ONLY by generate_checkout_abandonment_data.py to fabricate realistic-looking outcomes for this project's synthetic test data, exactly like decline_policy.json's simulated_success_rate. It has no effect on the real gate decision or any real Razorpay call.

otp_delay_or_failure.description: The customer reached OTP/3-D Secure authentication but it timed out, failed, or never arrived - a technical/delivery problem, not a customer decision

payment_method_unsupported.description: The customer's preferred or only payment method was not accepted, or failed validation, at method-selection or card-entry stage

price_shock.description: The customer reached final review/confirm, saw the total amount, and abandoned - a price-sensitivity signal, not a technical failure

distraction_or_multitasking.description: Nothing about the checkout itself appears to have caused the abandonment - the customer was likely pulled away and is plausibly still interested

trust_or_security_concern.description: Signals suggest the customer hesitated specifically over sharing payment details (often a new customer, often at the card-entry step) - pushing further risks looking predatory, not helpful
